candidate_relations.reason: The history is progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue atrophy, and MND on EMG, not progressive non-fluent aphasia.
Cognitive impairment plus clinical and EMG motor neuron disease is the same final object as FTLD-MND, with ALS-FTD as a harmless clinical alias.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: ALS-FTD is the clinical alias of FTLD-MND

candidate_relations.reason: Tongue atrophy, genioglossus MND, and a pathogenic TBK1 variant are not the corticobasal degeneration phenotype.
TBK1-linked FTD with DAT-scan parkinsonism is related but omits the required motor neuron disease component.
TBK1-associated FTD names the gene and cognitive syndrome but omits motor neuron disease.
Frontotemporal dementia with ALS and a TBK1 mutation states the same FTLD-MND object; added parkinsonism is compatible with the DAT-scan findings.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: FTD-ALS with TBK1 includes the required FTLD-MND object

candidate_relations.reason: Bulbar MND is documented, but amyotrophic lateral sclerosis alone omits frontotemporal lobar degeneration.
FTD-parkinsonism linked to chromosome 3 is CHMP2B disease and conflicts with the documented TBK1 variant.
Frontotemporal dementia captures the cognitive component but omits motor neuron disease.
Vertical gaze palsy raises PSP, but tongue atrophy, restricted facial/tongue EMG, and TBK1 mutation are not PSP.
Frontotemporal lobar degeneration is the parent of FTLD-MND and lacks the motor neuron disease component.
FTD with parkinsonism fits DAT-scan loss but omits the required MND.
Frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism-17 refers to MAPT/chr17 disease, not TBK1.
TBK1 maps to chromosome 12, so this locus is related, but the label is FTD-parkinsonism without motor neuron disease.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Chromosome 12 locus related to TBK1, still missing MND

candidate_relations.reason: FTD with parkinsonism-17 is a MAPT-linked subtype incompatible with the documented TBK1 variant.
Frontotemporal lobar degeneration with motor neuron disease is the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Same diagnostic object as the reference

The presentation is dysarthria, dysphagia, and MND rather than primary progressive aphasia.
Gaze palsy and DAT loss can mimic PSP-parkinsonism, but MND and TBK1 define FTLD-MND instead.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: PSP-parkinsonism unsupported as the final object

candidate_relations.reason: Frontotemporal dementia with motor neuron disease is the same final object as FTLD-MND.
